hints: Focus on what Fehling's solution is really testing for, which carbonyl type gives that brick-red precipitate?
For formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$, an aldehyde must be $\text{RCHO}$ where R is a $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9$ group, so start by listing the different butyl groups.
Count how many distinct ways you can attach the $\text{CHO}$ group to a 4-carbon skeleton, remembering straight chains and all branched versions.
walkthrough:
**Decode the Fehling's test**

Great start, let's see what the question is asking for. Fehling's solution gives a brick-red precipitate of $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$ only with aldehydes.

$$\text{RCHO + 2Cu}^{2+} + 5\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{RCOO}^- + \text{Cu}_2\text{O} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Ketones do not react, so we only need to count aldehyde isomers.

**Set up the aldehyde formula**

An aldehyde is $\text{R-CHO}$. The $\text{CHO}$ part already uses one C, one H and one O.

That leaves $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9$ for R. So every isomer is a different $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9$ group joined to $\text{CHO}$.

**Count the four butyl skeletons**

Now draw all the different $\text{C}_4$ arrangements around the $\text{CHO}$ carbon:

1. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ (pentanal)
2. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CHO}$ (2-methylbutanal)
3. $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CHO}$ (3-methylbutanal)
4. $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCHO}$ (2,2-dimethylpropanal)
That is 4 distinct structural isomers, all aldehydes, all positive to Fehling's.

options.A: Incorrect. This counts only pentanal, the straight-chain aldehyde. It forgets that the $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9$ group itself has branched isomers which give different aldehydes.
options.B: Incorrect. This might count the straight chain plus one branched example. There are more than two ways to arrange four carbons around a $\text{CHO}$ group.
options.C: Incorrect. This is the most common trap. Students find the three isomers with no quaternary carbon and miss $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCHO}$, where the $\text{CHO}$ is attached to a tertiary butyl group.
options.D: Correct. All four $\text{C}_5$ aldehydes, pentanal, 2-methylbutanal, 3-methylbutanal and 2,2-dimethylpropanal, have formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$ and reduce Fehling's solution to red $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$.
